title: Peach and Blackberry Galette
changes_from_base: A free-form galette of peaches and blackberries baked in plain shortcrust, with no crème pâtissière.
summary: A simple galette: hand-rubbed shortcrust folded around sugared peaches and blackberries and baked until bubbling.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
cold unsalted butter, in 1 cm cubes
iced water, plus 1 tbsp for brushing
ripe peaches, stoned and cut into 1 cm wedges

steps.title: Rub in
steps.text: put the flour and salt in the bowl, add the butter and rub it in with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs with a few pea-sized bits. Small lumps of butter left in the dough make the pastry flaky.

steps.title: Bring together
steps.text: sprinkle over 90 ml of the iced water and press with the spatula until the dough holds, adding up to 1 tbsp more only if it stays dry. Pat into a 10 cm disc, wrap and chill 1 h.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) with a shelf just below the middle, and line the tray. Leave the dough out 10 min, then roll it to a 30 cm round and lift it onto the tray.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: toss the peaches and blackberries with 60 g of the sugar. Pile them in the middle, leaving a 5 cm rim of bare pastry.

steps.title: Pleat
steps.text: fold the rim up over the fruit, overlapping it every 5 cm, and pinch the folds lightly without pressing them into the fruit.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: brush the pastry with 1 tbsp water and scatter the last 15 g sugar over pastry and fruit. Bake 45-50 min, until the pastry is deep golden and the juices bubble.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: leave on the tray 10 min, loosen with the fish slice, slide onto the rack and cool another 30 min before cutting. The juices thicken as the galette cools.

tips: Use peaches that are ripe but still firm so the wedges keep their shape.
Frozen blackberries work; add them straight from the freezer.
If the dough cracks as you fold, pinch it back together; the rustic look is the point.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day. Keep leftovers covered at room temperature overnight and warm in a 180 °C oven for 10 min.
